query: Consider the following context: Conventional material processing approaches often achieve strengthening of materials at the cost of reduced ductility. In that context, which method can be used for overcome the strength-ductility trade-off, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The strength-ductility trade-off in conventional materials can be overcome by using high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with optimized composition and processing methods.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional materials with limited strength and ductility
generation.intervention: Design and processing of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with optimized composition and methods
generation.conditions: Room and high temperatures, various loading conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructure, phase composition, and lattice parameter of constituent atoms
generation.mechanism: Solid solution hardening, precipitation hardening, and grain refinement
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced strength and ductility, improved high-temperature stability and properties
generation.baseline: Conventional materials with limited strength and ductility
generation.boundary: Optimized composition and processing methods for HEAs
generation.uncertainty: Limited understanding of the underlying mechanisms and optimal design strategies for HEAs

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of HEAs with varying composition and processing methods
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized HEAs do not exhibit enhanced strength and ductility compared to conventional materials, the hypothesis is falsified.
